info.title: SOVD x-update extension
info.description:
The x-update vendor extensions to ISO 17978-3 §7.18 (software update) and §7.19 (entity status and restart), as in `docs/x-update.md`. Paths are relative to `/vehicle/v1` or `/v1` (both served); where the trees differ, the operation says so. The orchestrator addresses updates on the node level: `{entity}` is the node, the collection is `/updates` and every registration names its executor as `target`, one of the node's `x-update.update-targets` (`GET /`). Each executor is an entity of its own — a top-level component, or a subcomponent of the node where the server serves a tree — whose document reports `software_update` and `capabilities.x-update.verdict`. Executors here are said to be IDLE while they hold no update. Standard operations are shown only where x-update adds to them. The node operations and `data/x-update-state` are served by the embedding machine manager.

Not in this version: executors that need a verdict refusing `automated` with 409; retiring the x-ota names; executor-side recording of the update id.

Not implemented yet in SOVDd: adopting (until then a verdict, `prepare` or `execute` on an update only the executor holds answers 404) and keeping a transaction atomic (the backend's part).

get.summary: Node capability document (§7.6.3) with the x-update update targets
get.description: The node scope. `updates` links the node-level collection; `x-update.update-targets` lists the executors an update may name as `target`. A node without update executors advertises neither.

parameters.name: component_id
parameters.description: The executor: one of the node's `update-targets`.

get.summary: Executor entity body (§7.6): software_update and the x-update capability flag
get.description: An executor is an entity of its own: a top-level component, or a subcomponent of the node where the server serves an entity tree (then under `/components/{node}/subcomponents/{executor}`). Its standard capabilities report `software_update`; `capabilities.x-update.verdict` tells whether `execute` awaits a verdict.

get.summary: List the updates the server holds (§7.18.2)
get.description: By the client's id. The server rebuilds the list from its executor, so a client that lost its state finds its updates by id after a server or executor restart. Required: without listing and adopting, a client that lost its state cannot find and settle its updates.

post.description: The client gives the id; the server keeps it verbatim and never replaces or derives one (under `/v1` it creates one when none is given). A registration with an id the executor still holds adopts that update instead of starting a new one (201, `x-update.adopted: true`); the same id with a different manifest is refused with 409.

400.description: No id (under `/vehicle/v1`), an empty id, or an invalid body

409.description: The id is held with a different manifest

get.description: An update only the executor holds is described with the id as its name and the size of its held parts.

delete.description: Before `execute` (REGISTERED, PREPARING, PREPARED) it discards what the executor staged, aborting a running `prepare`; the software in use is never touched. Once the update has settled (COMMITTED, ROLLED_BACK or FAILED) it removes the record. Synchronous: 204 once the update is gone. There is no finish verb and no revert verb. Under `/v1` it is refused with 405 while the update runs in phase execute (EXECUTING, EXECUTED, COMMITTING, ROLLING_BACK), ISO 17978-3 §7.18.8; `/vehicle/v1` deletes it, aborting the running step.

405.description: `method-not-allowed` (under `/v1`): in phase execute and not settled; wait, or send the verdict first

post.description: The body is the part's bytes, streamed as is (not multipart). `Content-Disposition` is required and names the part: its `filename` parameter, else its `name`; the name is the part's URL segment (not empty, no `/`, not `.` or `..`). `Content-Type` is recorded as the part's mimetype (default `application/octet-stream`). Uploading a part of the same name again replaces it. Parts are accepted while the update is registered or uploading.

409.description: The update no longer accepts parts

put.summary: Upload a part, named by the path (legacy alias of the POST; scheduled for deprecation)

get.summary: Read a part back as it was uploaded
get.description: A client retrying an upload checks with it whether its last one landed (lib-orchestrate reads `bulk-data/manifest` before it uploads the L2, and accepts only 200 with the same bytes, or 404). The server keeps the bytes of an update's parts up to 1 MiB together, enough for a manifest.

200.description: The part's bytes, with its recorded `Content-Type`

404.description: No such part, or no such update

501.description: A part beyond what the server keeps: only the executor holds its bytes

put.summary: Prepare (§7.18.5): verify and stage; the update goes PREPARING, then PREPARED

409.description: Not in a state `prepare` is accepted in, or the executor is busy

put.summary: Execute (§7.18.6): arm the new software; the update goes EXECUTING, then EXECUTED
put.description: The restart that activates the new software happens outside this contract: whoever is authorized issues `PUT {entity}/status/restart` (§7.19), or a power cycle does it. The client awaits EXECUTED.

409.description: Not PREPARED, or the executor is busy

get.summary: Update status (§7.18.7) with the x-update member

put.description: Accepted in EXECUTED; again in COMMITTED, where it changes nothing. The update moves to COMMITTING. For an update whose `verdict_scope` is `update`. A member of a node transaction (`verdict_scope` `node`) is settled by the node operation; under `/v1` a per-update verdict on it answers 409 before any state check, naming the node operations, and `/vehicle/v1` accepts it for existing clients. Each update reports its own state as it actually is. On an update only the executor holds (after a server restart), EXECUTING or EXECUTED, it adopts the update: the server registers it again as executed and staged for its reset, and the verdict then settles it; held in another state, it answers 404.

404.description: Unknown update, or one the executor holds in a state no verdict adopts

409.description: `precondition-not-fulfilled`: not in a state the verb is accepted in, or (under `/v1`) a member of a node transaction

put.description: Accepted in EXECUTING and EXECUTED; again in ROLLED_BACK, where it changes nothing. The update moves to ROLLING_BACK. Valid for every update; see `x-update-commit` on transactions. On an update only the executor holds (after a server restart), EXECUTING or EXECUTED, it adopts the update: the server registers it again as executed and staged for its reset, and the verdict then settles it; held in another state, it answers 404.

404.description: Unknown update, or one the executor holds in a state no verdict adopts

409.description: `precondition-not-fulfilled`: not in a state the verb is accepted in, or (under `/v1`) a member of a node transaction

post.summary: Node commit: every component in the node's open transaction, all or nothing
post.description: Settles every component in the node's open transaction, all or nothing: the verdict for updates whose `verdict_scope` is `node`. Served by the embedding machine manager, not by SOVDd. On a server configured as one node they are the node's own, `/components/{node}/operations/x-update-commit/executions`: the embedding machine manager mounts them there and not at the root, and the `/v1` 409 of a per-update verdict on a member names that path.

200.description: The verdict was applied; `result.committed` lists the components

post.summary: Node rollback: every component in the node's open transaction, all or nothing
post.description: Settles every component in the node's open transaction, all or nothing: the verdict for updates whose `verdict_scope` is `node`. Served by the embedding machine manager, not by SOVDd. On a server configured as one node they are the node's own, `/components/{node}/operations/x-update-rollback/executions`: the embedding machine manager mounts them there and not at the root, and the `/v1` 409 of a per-update verdict on a member names that path.

200.description: The verdict was applied; `result.rolled_back` lists the components

get.description: Served by the embedding machine manager, not by SOVDd. The same body as `x-ota-update-state`, plus `node_boot_id`.

XUpdateState.description:
The update's state, named after the verb that leads to it (REGISTERED after registration under `/v1`, READY under `/vehicle/v1`). Total; the standard `phase`/`status` in the same body agree with it:

| state | phase | status | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| IDLE | — | — | the entity holds no update; not an update's state, but the one its entity reports; `POST` registers one |
| REGISTERED | prepare | pending | registered; manifest and parts may be uploaded; `prepare` or `DELETE` |
| PREPARING | prepare | inProgress | verifying and staging |
| PREPARED | prepare | completed | staged in the inactive bank; `execute` or `DELETE` |
| EXECUTING | execute | inProgress | armed; the restart named by `reset_kind` has not been observed yet |
| EXECUTED | execute | inProgress | the new software runs; a verdict is awaited |
| COMMITTING | execute | inProgress | commit accepted and running |
| COMMITTED | execute | completed | permanent; `DELETE` |
| ROLLING_BACK | execute | inProgress | rollback accepted and running (the client's, or the executor's own, e.g. after failed trial boots) |
| ROLLED_BACK | execute | failed | the previous software is in effect again; `DELETE` |
| FAILED | prepare or execute | failed | see the standard error object; `DELETE` |

adopted.description: Present, and true, on an update a registration adopted.

reset_kind.description: What must restart to activate the update: none, a standard restart of this entity, or one restart of the node's entity for every update on the node that reports `node`. The x-ota member `x-ota-reset-kind` keeps its old vocabulary beside it.

target.description: Under `/v1` only: the component the update is registered on.

verdict_scope.description: Under `/v1` only: `update`, settled by its own `x-update-commit` / `x-update-rollback`; `node`, a member of a node transaction, settled only by the node operations (a per-update verdict is refused with 409). Independent of `reset_kind`.

id.description: Chosen by the client; kept verbatim. Under `/v1` a registration without it gets a server-created UUID (ISO 17978-3 §7.18.9), returned in `Location`, `id` and `update_id`; `/vehicle/v1` refuses it with 400. An empty `id` is refused with 400 on both trees.

target.description: The executor the update is for: one of the node's `update-targets`. On an entity-level collection it must name that entity.

sha256.description: Of the uploaded part; for a part only the executor holds, the executor's digest.

href.description: Absent for a part only the executor holds.

present.description: Whether the executor already holds the part, matched by name (`name` or `#name`), not by hash.

Component.description: Standard entity body of an executor subcomponent; only the x-update capability is shown.

verdict.description: true: `execute` stops at EXECUTED and a verdict is required. false: `execute` commits on its own. Absent: the server cannot tell. There is no request option for it; `automated` asks the executor to decide for itself.

verdict_scope.description: Under `/v1`: how this executor's updates are settled; see the status member.

updates.description: The node-level updates collection (`/updates`). Absent on a node without update executors.

update-targets.description: The executors of the node; a registration's `target` is one of them.
